title: Even the holiest sin daily
source_text: XVII. Verum non solum homines sunt per naturam peccato immersi, & per legem peccati convicti: sed etiam postquam sunt per gratiam renati, multum ab eo absunt ut undiquaque perfectum obsequium legi praestent. Etenim sanctissimi quique in multa peccata quotidie labuntur: Juxta illud Jacobi, In multis offendimus omnes. [marg.: Jac. 3.] Et Joannis epistola prima cap. 1. Si dixerimus quod peccatum non habemus, ipsi nos seducimus, & veritas in nobis non est. Quibus congruit quod pronunciat sapiens, Eccl. cap. 7. Non est homo justus in terra qui faciat bonum, & non peccet.
pass_a_gloss: XVII. But not only are men by nature sunk in sin, & convicted of sin by the law: but even after they are reborn through grace, they are far from rendering to the law an obedience perfect in every way. For all the holiest fall daily into many sins: According to that saying of James, In many things we all offend. [margin: Jas. 3] And John's first epistle chap. 1. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, & the truth is not in us. With which agrees what the wise man pronounces, Eccl. chap. 7. There is not a righteous man on earth who does good, & does not sin.
pass_b_english: Thesis XVII. Not only are people sunk in sin by nature and convicted of sin by the law; even after they are reborn by grace, they are far from giving the law a perfect obedience in every respect. Even the holiest fall into many sins every day.

So James says, 'We all stumble in many things' (margin: Jas. 3), and John in chapter 1 of his first epistle, 'If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.' The wise man agrees in Ecclesiastes 7: 'There is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.'

lemmas.gloss: an obedience perfect in every way
In many things we all offend

choices.why: Le Blanc's strict sense: satisfying the law in every respect, according to its full rigour.
